'''Francis Stanley Kaminsky III'''<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Pablo S.|last=Torre|title=Wisconsin Badgers big man Frank Kaminsky is back for senior season|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/feature/story/_/id/11822147/Wisconsin-badgers-big-man-frank-kaminsky-back-senior-season|magazine=ESPN The Magazine|date=November 5, 2014|access-date=November 5, 2014}}</ref> (born April 4, 1993) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Alvark Tokyo]] of the Japanese [[B.League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin Badgers]].

During his college career, Kaminsky set the Wisconsin single-game record for points (43).<ref>{{cite news|title=Wisconsin's Frank Kaminsky nets school record 43 points in rout|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2013/11/19/wisconsin-frank-kaminsky-school-record-43-points-north-dakota/3647683/|newspaper=USA Today|agency=Associated Press|date=November 19, 2013|access-date=November 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Elena|last=Bergeron|title=Three and change|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10172331/wisconsin-badgers-frank-kaminsky-thank-scoring-success-espn-magazine|work=ESPN.com|date=December 27, 2013|access-date=June 26, 2015}}</ref> He was the unanimous men's [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|National College Player of the Year]] in 2015. Kaminsky was drafted ninth overall by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the [[2015 NBA draft]]. He played with Charlotte for four seasons before signing with the [[Phoenix Suns]] as a free agent in July 2019. With the Suns, he reached the [[NBA Finals]] in 2021.

==Early life==
Kaminsky's father, Frank Jr., played basketball at [[Lewis University]]. His mother, Mary, played volleyball at [[Northwestern University|Northwestern]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.uwbadgers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=153 |title=Frank Kaminsky Bio |publisher=uwbadgers.com |access-date=April 5, 2015}}</ref> Kaminsky, who is of Polish and Serbian ancestry,<ref>[https://www.nba.com/hornets/alongside-local-legends-kaminsky-ventures-basketball-crazed-serbia Alongside Local Legends, Kaminsky Ventures to Basketball-Crazed Serbia]</ref> grew up in [[Woodridge, Illinois]] in a [[Serbian Americans|Serbian community]].<ref>[http://patch.com/illinois/woodridge/wisconsin-badgers-frank-kaminskys-childhood-home-hits-market-0 Wisconsin Badgers' Frank Kaminsky's Childhood Home Hits the Market – Woodridge, IL Patch] Retrieved 2017-02-19.</ref><ref name=Wagerbop>{{cite news |url=https://www.wagerbop.com/suns-frank-kaminsky-might-play-for-the-serbian-national-team/ |title=Suns' Frank Kaminsky Might Play For the Serbian National Team |access-date=February 16, 2020 |date=November 24, 2019 |work=wagerbop.com}}</ref> In 1998, when he was 5 years old, his aunt [[Karen Stack Umlauf]] and uncle [[Jim Stack]] worked for the [[Chicago Bulls]], and he had access to the practice facility when [[Michael Jordan]], [[Scottie Pippen]] and [[Dennis Rodman]] were on the team.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10866360/frank-kaminsky-wisconsin-badgers-says-nba-looks-boring |title=Frank Kaminsky: Badgers to be great |access-date=May 1, 2014 |date=May 1, 2014 |work=ESPN}}</ref> Until high school, Kaminsky participated in basketball tournaments organized by Serb National Federation as a member of the Serbian Eagles A.C.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://kosarka.hotsport.rs/2018/08/16/kaminski-u-beogradu-tacno-je-imam-srpske-korene-poceo-sam-u-srpskoj-ligi-u-cikagu/ |title=Kaminski u Beogradu: Tačno je, imam srpske korene – počeo sam u srpskoj ligi u Čikagu! |access-date=September 3, 2019 |date=August 18, 2019 |work=kosarka.hotsport.rs|language=sr}}</ref><ref name=Wagerbop />

Kaminsky attended [[Benet Academy]] in [[Lisle, Illinois]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Campbell |first=Alex |date=5 May 2020 |title=Frank Kaminsky From Prep Star to NBA |url=https://www.nctv17.org/news/frank-kaminsky-from-prep-star-to-nba/ |access-date=12 June 2023 |website=Naperville Community Television/NCTV17}}</ref> He was named first-team all-state by the [[Chicago Sun-Times]] and IBCA and second-team all-state by the [[Associated Press|AP]] after averaging 14.2 points, 8.7 rebounds, 4.2 blocks and 2.8 assists during his senior season. He led the Redwings to a 29–1 season after being defeated in the Sectional Semifinals by the East Aurora Tomcats that were led by Connecticut Huskies superstar and National Champion [[Ryan Boatright]]. He was also named all-area, all-conference and [[East Suburban Catholic Conference]] Player of the Year. Kaminsky's jersey number, 44, was retired in a ceremony at Benet Academy on November 18, 2017.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/naperville-sun/ct-nvs-boys-basketball-benet-frank-kaminsky-st-1119-20171118-story.html|title=Homecoming king: Frank Kaminsky returns to Benet for banner raising|last=Baumgartner|first=Blake|work=Naperville Sun|access-date=2017-11-19|language=en-US}}</ref>

Kaminsky has stated that his family had [[Chicago White Sox]] season tickets when he was a child and has described himself as a "die-hard White Sox fan." He threw out the first pitch at a White Sox game against the St. Louis Cardinals on July 21, 2015, stating in a pre-game interview that a saying in his family was, "We have two favorite teams in the MLB, the White Sox and whoever is playing the Cubs."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2015/7/21/18574390/white-sox-fan-frank-kaminsky-throws-out-first-pitch-at-cell|title = White Sox fan Frank Kaminsky throws out first pitch at Cell|date = July 21, 2015}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Frank Kaminsky 2012.jpg|thumb|Kaminsky with [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]] in 2012]]

Kaminsky played in 35 of 36 games as a freshman. He scored a season-high nine points against [[UMKC Kangaroos men's basketball|UMKC]] on November 22, 2011.

Kaminsky played in 32 games, starting the first two games of the season. He finished the season averaging 4.2 points and 1.8 rebounds per game. He led the team in free-throw percentage at 76.7%. He posted a season-high 19 points at [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] on February 3, 2013.

On November 19, 2013, Kaminsky broke the Wisconsin single-game scoring record with 43 points against [[University of North Dakota men's basketball|North Dakota]].<ref>{{cite web |title=School Record 43 points from Frank Kaminsky power UW past North Dakota |date=November 20, 2013 |url=http://host.madison.com/sports/college/basketball/men/badgers-men-s-basketball-school-record-points-from-frank-kaminsky/article_f05e4e99-486c-5332-bdbb-77b253f436a0.html |publisher=Madison.com |access-date=December 26, 2013}}</ref> Kaminsky shot 16 of 19 from the field, including six of six from 3-point range and five of six from the free throw line. The previous Wisconsin single-game record was 42 points, set by Ken Barnes (vs. [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] on March 8, 1965) and [[Michael Finley]] (vs. [[Eastern Michigan Eagles men's basketball|Eastern Michigan]] on December 10, 1994).

At the conclusion of the regular season, Kaminsky was named first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031014aag.html |title=Big Ten Announces 2014 Men's Basketball Postseason Honors: Michigan's Stauskas named Big Ten Player of the Year |access-date=March 10, 2014 |date=March 10, 2014 |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |work=BigTen.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180429211627/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031014aag.html |archive-date=April 29, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On March 29, 2014, Kaminsky scored 28 points and had 11 rebounds as Wisconsin defeated #1 seeded [[2013–14 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] 64–63 in overtime during the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] to advance to the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|Final Four]]. After the game, Kaminsky was named West Regional Most Outstanding Player.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/-college-basketball-mens-tournament/news/20140402/frank-kaminsky-bo-ryan-wisconsin-final-four/ |title=In a family of athletes, Frank Kaminsky Jr. finally finds his moment |access-date=April 3, 2014 |date=April 2, 2014 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |first=Lindsay |last=Schnell |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140405082359/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/-college-basketball-mens-tournament/news/20140402/frank-kaminsky-bo-ryan-wisconsin-final-four/ |archive-date=April 5, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Ahead of the 2014 season, Kaminsky was named the Big Ten preseason player of the year.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.jsonline.com/blogs/sports/279414882.html |title=Frank Kaminsky named Big Ten preseason player of the year |first=Jeff |last=Potrykus |newspaper=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel |date=October 16, 2014}}</ref> The Badgers were unanimously picked to win the Big Ten Championship.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.foxsports.com/wisconsin/story/badgers-unanimous-pick-to-win-big-ten-basketball-title-101614 |title=Wisconsin Badgers unanimous pick to win Big Ten basketball title |work=FOX Sports |first=Jesse |last=Temple |date=October 16, 2014}}</ref>

The Badgers and Kaminsky validated those predictions. The Badgers had a 36–3 record in games Kaminsky played. They won the [[List of Big Ten Conference men's basketball regular season champions|Big Ten regular season title]] with a 16–2 record and the [[2015 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament title]]. After becoming the first NCAA tournament 1-seed in school history, they made their way to their second consecutive [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#Final Four|Final Four]]. There, they avenged their previous season's loss to Kentucky, upsetting the 38–0 Wildcats 71–64 behind Kaminsky's 20 points and 11 rebounds.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2015/4/4/8346033/kentucky-wisconsin-2015-final-four-results-final-score-frank-kaminsky-karl-anthony-towns|title=Wisconsin stuns Kentucky, moves on to title game|work=SBNation.com|access-date=2017-08-29}}</ref> In the Badgers' first national championship game in 74 years, they lost a 9-point second-half lead and were defeated 68–63 by the Duke Blue Devils.  Kaminsky finished with 21 points and 12 rebounds. For the season, he finished with 18.8 PPG and 8.2 RPG, despite playing for a team that ranked 346th out of 351 in adjusted tempo. He led the nation in PER, an efficiency-based stat. Wisconsin boasted the highest adjusted offensive efficiency in [[Ken Pomeroy|KenPom]] history.

Kaminsky was named [[2015 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|consensus first-team All-American]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/033015aac.html |title=AP honor makes Kaminsky a consensus All-American |date=March 30, 2015 |publisher=uwbadgers.com }}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> On March 31, 2015, he was named the [[NABC Player of the Year|National Association of Basketball Coaches Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/033115aaa.html |title=Kaminsky Named NABC POY |publisher=Big Ten Conference |date=March 31, 2015 |access-date=April 5, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402130901/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/033115aaa.html |archive-date=April 2, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On April 3 he was named [[Associated Press College Basketball Player of the Year]], the first Wisconsin player to receive the award since its creation in 1961.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/2015/04/03/wisconsins-frank-kaminsky-chosen-ap-player-year/25247945/ |title=Wisconsin's Frank Kaminsky chosen AP Player of the Year |agency=Associated Press |date=April 3, 2015 |newspaper=Indianapolis Star}}</ref> He also received the [[Oscar Robertson Trophy]] as the United States Basketball Writers Association College Player of the Year.<ref>[https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2419025-frank-kaminsky-wins-2015-oscar-robertson-mens-college-player-of-the-year-award Frank Kaminsky Wins 2015 Oscar Robertson, Associated Press Player of Year Awards]. Bleacher Report (2015-04-03). Retrieved on 2015-11-07.</ref> On April 5, he was named the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].<ref>[https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2420039-frank-kaminsky-named-2015-naismith-mens-college-player-of-the-year Frank Kaminsky Named 2015 Naismith Men's College Player of the Year]. Bleacher Report. Retrieved on 2015-11-07.</ref> On April 10, he won both the [[John R. Wooden Award]] and [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar Center of the Year Award]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/wisconsin-badgers-frank-kaminsky-wins-center-of-the-year-041015 |title=Kaminsky adds more hardware, wins Center of Year award |work=Fox Sports |date=April 10, 2015}}</ref> On June 12 Kaminsky was named University of Wisconsin's Male Athlete of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.uwbadgers.com/genrel/061215aab.html |title=Kaminsky, Martin named UW's Athletes of the Year |publisher=uwbadgers.com |date=June 12, 2015 |access-date=June 18, 2015 |archive-date=October 12, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151012212858/http://www.uwbadgers.com/genrel/061215aab.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He graduated with a life sciences communication major that same year. In 2015, the [[National Polish-American Sports Hall of Fame]] awarded its NPASHF Excellence in Sports Award to Kaminsky.

==Professional career==
===Charlotte Hornets (2015–2019)===
On June 25, 2015, Kaminsky was selected with the ninth overall pick by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the [[2015 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets Select Frank Kaminsky with No. 9 Pick in 2015 NBA Draft|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-select-frank-kaminsky-no-9-pick-2015-nba-draft|access-date=June 26, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=June 25, 2015}}</ref> On December 2, he scored 16 points in a 116–99 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]], earning increased minutes with starting center [[Al Jefferson]] out injured.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Curry scores 40, Warriors top Hornets 116–99 to go 20–0 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151202/GSWCHA/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151203014303/http://www.nba.com/games/20151202/GSWCHA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2015-12-03 |access-date=2015-12-03 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On December 23, he scored a then career-high 23 points in a 102–89 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Olynyk scores 20 as Celtics hold off Hornets, win |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151223/BOSCHA/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151227005504/http://www.nba.com/games/20151223/BOSCHA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2015-12-27 |access-date=2015-12-24 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On December 30, he had his second 20-point outing of the season in a 122–117 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Frank Kaminsky 2015–16 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/k/kaminfr01/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=2021-07-13 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On April 10, 2016, he recorded 18 points and a then career-high 11 rebounds in a 113–98 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gortat scores 21 points as Wizards upset Hornets, 113–98 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160410/CHAWAS/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160410205801/http://www.nba.com/games/20160410/CHAWAS/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2016-04-10 |access-date=2016-04-11 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> In Game 3 of the Hornets' first-round playoff series against the [[Miami Heat]], Kaminsky scored 15 points in a 96–80 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hornets snap 14-year playoff drought, beat Heat 96–80 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160423/MIACHA/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160424065558/http://www.nba.com/games/20160423/MIACHA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2016-04-24 |access-date=2016-04-24 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

On November 21, 2016, Kaminsky tied a career high with 23 points on 9-of-11 shooting in a 105–90 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 21, 2016 |title=Grizzlies vs. Hornets – Game Recap – November 21, 2016 – ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400899651 |access-date=2021-07-13 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On February 1, 2017, he set a new career high with 24 points off the bench in a 126–111 loss to the Golden State Warriors.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 2, 2017 |title=Stephen Curry's 3-point clinic leads Warriors past Hornets |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899435 |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref> He topped that mark on February 15, scoring 27 points in a 90–85 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>[http://www.fanragsports.com/news/hornets-frank-kaminsky-sets-new-career-high-scoring/ Hornets' Frank Kaminsky sets new career-high in scoring]</ref> On February 25, he recorded 23 points and a career-high 13 rebounds in a 99–85 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref name="Kaminsky2017">{{Cite web |title=Frank Kaminsky 2016–17 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/k/kaminfr01/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=2021-07-13 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On April 8, he recorded a then career-high 7 assists in a loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref name="Kaminsky2017" />

On November 20, 2017, Kaminsky scored a season-high 24 points in a 118–102 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Frank Kaminsky 2017–18 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/k/kaminfr01/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=2021-07-13 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On December 18, he scored 24 points in a 109–91 win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975192 Kaminsky ties season-high with 24, Hornets top Knicks 109–91]</ref> On April 10, 2018, he scored 24 points in a 119–93 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975959 Hornets take advantage of resting Pacers for 119–93 win]</ref>

On November 21, 2018, after scoring just nine points over the Hornets' first 16 games of the 2018–19 season, Kaminsky had 11 points off the bench in a 127–109 win over the Pacers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 21, 2018 |title=Lamb scores 21, Hornets topple Pacers 127–109 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070933 |access-date=November 21, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> He lost his spot in the rotation in [[2018–19 Charlotte Hornets season|2018–19]] under new coach [[James Borrego]], appearing in just 26 games at the conclusion of February.<ref name="hornets-nets">{{Cite web |date=March 1, 2019 |title=Hornets end skid at 3, roll to 123–112 victory over Nets |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071602 |access-date=March 2, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On March 1, 2019, he was inserted into the rotation to combat [[zone defense]] with his passing ability, going on to score 15 points in a 123–112 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref name="hornets-nets" /> On April 5, he recorded 22 points and 13 rebounds in a 113–111 win over the Raptors.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 5, 2019 |title=Lamb hits 3-point winner, Hornets beat Raptors 113–111 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071853 |access-date=April 8, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Two days later, he scored a season-high 24 points in a 104–91 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 7, 2019 |title=Walker-led Hornets top Pistons 104–91, holding playoff hopes |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071871 |access-date=April 8, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2019–2022)===
On July 17, 2019, Kaminsky signed a two-year, $10 million deal with the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Suns Sign Frank Kaminsky III|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-frank-kaminsky-iii|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 13, 2020|date=July 17, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Feldman|first1=Dan|title=Report: Suns signing Frank Kaminsky for room exception|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/report-suns-signing-frank-kaminsky-211335248.html|website=sports.yahoo.com|access-date=February 13, 2020|date=July 1, 2019|archive-date=February 13, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200213132702/https://sports.yahoo.com/report-suns-signing-frank-kaminsky-211335248.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first= Hunter|last=Hippel|title=New Suns PF Frank Kaminsky details his free agency process|url= https://arizonasports.com/story/2015503/new-suns-pf-frank-kaminsky-details-his-free-agency-process/|publisher=Arizona Sports 98.7FM|date= 19 July 2019|access-date= 4 September 2020}}</ref> Kaminsky scored a season-high 24 points in a 115–108 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on December 11. Entering 2020, Kaminsky was initially sidelined with a right knee injury before having a left patella stress fracture sideline him for most of the rest of the season. He returned to action during the [[2020 NBA Bubble]] period on July 31, 2020, helping the Suns with a 125–112 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20200731/PHXWAS/#/recap|title=Booker scores 27 points, Suns beat Wizards 125–112 in return|website=NBA.com|date=July 31, 2020|access-date=July 31, 2020}}</ref> Kaminsky ultimately helped the team  by coming off the bench for the majority of the rest of the season, ending with a record of 8–0  in the [[2020 NBA Bubble]], with Phoenix thus having a winning streak of at least eight games for the first time since March 2010.<ref>{{cite web|title=Booker's 35 points help streaking Suns beat 76ers 130–117|url=https://www.nba.com/game/phx-vs-phi-0021901299|website=NBA.com |date=August 11, 2020|access-date=August 17, 2020}}</ref>

On November 19, 2020, Kaminsky had his second year on his contract waived, entering free agency early. On November 29, Kaminsky signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings Sign Frank Kaminsky|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-frank-kaminsky|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 1, 2020|date=November 30, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Anderson|first1=Jason|title=Source: Sacramento Kings sign free agent center Frank 'The Tank' Kaminsky to one-year deal|url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/article247448265.html|website=sacbee.com|access-date=December 1, 2020|date=November 26, 2020}}</ref> but was later waived by the Kings on December 20 after appearing in four preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings Waive Frank Kaminsky|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-waive-frank-kaminsky|date=December 20, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 20, 2020}}</ref> Once he cleared waivers, Kaminsky was re-signed by the Suns on a more team-friendly, one-year deal that season.<ref>{{cite tweet|last=Charania|first=Shams|user=ShamsCharania|number=1341232720102510599|date=December 21, 2020|title=The Phoenix Suns have claimed F/C Frank Kaminsky off free agency waivers, sources tell @TheAthleticNBA @Stadium.|language=en|access-date=January 29, 2021}}</ref> On January 28, 2021, he was two assists shy from a triple-double night, recording 12 points, 13 rebounds, and a career-high eight assists off the bench in a 114–93 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Suns Pull Away From Warriors, Climb Above .500 (Suns snap 3-game skid, roll to 114–93 win over Warriors)|first=David|last=Brandt|url=https://www.nba.com/game/gsw-vs-phx-0022000286|website=NBA.com|date=January 28, 2021|access-date=January 29, 2021}}</ref> Later moving up to a starting power forward role in February, Kaminsky had another near-triple-double performance on February 10 with 12 points, 8 rebounds, and a career high-tying eight assists in a close 125–124 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Suns Rally Past Bucks Despite 47 From Antetokounmpo (Suns rally to beat Bucks 125–124 despite Giannis' 47 points)|first=David|last=Brandt|url=https://www.nba.com/game/mil-vs-phx-0022000389|website=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2021|access-date=February 11, 2021}}</ref> Kaminsky reached his first [[2021 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], but the Suns lost the series in six games to the Bucks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2732471/suns-season-ends-with-loss-in-nba-finals-to-deserving-champion-bucks/|title=Suns' season ends with loss in NBA Finals to deserving champion Bucks|website=Arizona Sports 98.7 FM|last=Olson|first=Kellan|date=July 19, 2021|access-date=November 11, 2021}}</ref>

On August 4, 2021, Kaminsky re-signed with the Suns on a one-year, $1.2 million deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10009753-frank-kaminsky-suns-agree-to-1-year-21m-contract-in-free-agency|title=Frank Kaminsky, Suns Agree to 1-Year, $2.1M Contract in Free Agency|website=Bleacher Report|last=Goldberg|first=Rob|date=August 4, 2021|access-date=November 11, 2021}}</ref> On November 10, Kaminsky scored a career-high 31 points in a 119–109 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2021/11/11/phoenix-suns-win-portland-trail-blazers-frank-kaminsky-career-night/6381875001/|title=5 takeaways from Phoenix Suns' win over Trail Blazers on Frank Kaminsky's career night|last=Rankin|first=Duane|website=azcentral.com|date=November 10, 2021|access-date=November 11, 2021}}</ref> On November 21, he was diagnosed with a stress reaction in his right knee and was ruled out indefinitely.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Phoenix Suns' Frank Kaminsky out indefinitely with right knee injury |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32687407/phoenix-suns-frank-kaminsky-indefinitely-right-knee-injury |access-date=March 21, 2022 |website=ESPN|date=November 22, 2021 }}</ref> On January 6, 2022, Kaminsky underwent a procedure on his right knee and was ruled out for at least two months.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Suns' Frank Kaminsky has procedure on right knee, out at least 8 weeks |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2959253/suns-frank-kaminsky-has-procedure-on-right-knee-out-at-least-8-weeks/ |access-date=March 21, 2022 |website=[[KMVP-FM|Arizona Sports 98.7]]|date=January 8, 2022 }}</ref> On April 7, 2022, Kaminsky was waived.<ref>{{cite tweet|first=Duane|last=Rankin|number=1512200906284036096|title=Official: #Suns waive Frank Kaminsky III|user=DuaneRankin|date=April 7, 2022|access-date=April 7, 2022}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2022–2023)===
On July 12, 2022, Kaminsky signed a one-year deal with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hawks Sign Center Frank Kaminsky|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-center-frank-kaminsky|website=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2022|access-date=July 16, 2022}}</ref>

===Houston Rockets (2023)===
[[File:Frenk Kaminski 04.jpg|thumb|Kaminsky in 2023]]

On February 9, 2023, Kaminsky, [[Justin Holiday]], and two future second-round draft picks were traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for [[Bruno Fernando]] and [[Garrison Mathews]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rockets Complete Four-Player Trade with Atlanta|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-complete-four-player-trade-with-atlanta|website=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2023|access-date=February 9, 2023}}</ref>

===Partizan (2023–2024)===
On August 17, 2023, Kaminsky signed with [[KK Partizan|Partizan]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia]], the [[ABA League|Adriatic League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Frenk Kaminski nakon što je postao košarkaš Partizana Mozzart Bet: "Dolazim da se takmičim i pobeđujem"|url=https://kkpartizan.rs/sr/vest/3514/frenk-kaminski-je-novi-kosarkas-partizana-mozzart-bet|newspaper=Normacore.com|date=August 17, 2023|access-date=August 17, 2023|language=Serbian |last1=Normasoft. Net |first1=Normasoft }}</ref> In the [[EuroLeague]], he averaged 8.9 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.6 assists per game. The season was deemed to be unsuccessful for Partizan as they finished the season without lifting any trophy.<ref>{{cite news|title=Očekuje nas burno leto u Partizanu – ko ostaje, a ko odlazi?|url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/srpska-kosarka/28999/ocekuje-nas-burno-leto-u-partizanu-ko-ostaje-a-ko-odlazi/vest|date=June 6, 2024|access-date=June 11, 2024|language=Serbian}}</ref>

===Raptors 905 (2024–2025)===
On September 26, 2024, Kaminsky signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]],<ref>{{cite tweet|author=DANA|title=Official: Phoenix Suns sign bigs Frank Kaminsky, Mamadi Diakite, and rookie forward Moses Wood.|number=1839462137447731326|user=iam_DanaScott|date=September 26, 2024|access-date=September 27, 2024}}</ref> but was waived on October 19.<ref>{{cite tweet|first=Duane|last=Rankin|title=OFFICIAL: Suns waiving Frank Kaminsky. #Suns|number=1847768970189033613|user=DuaneRankin|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}}</ref>

On December 16, 2024, Kaminsky signed with the [[Raptors 905]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RAPTORS 905 ACQUIRE KAMINSKY III FROM WAIVER WIRE|url=https://raptors905.gleague.nba.com/news/raptors-905-acquire-kaminsky-iii-from-waiver-wire|website=NBA.com|date=December 16, 2024|access-date=December 16, 2024}}</ref> On March 16, 2025, it was announced that Kaminsky would miss the remainder of the season after undergoing [[arthroscopy|arthroscopic]] knee surgery.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Injury Notes: Washington, Ball, Thybulle, Kaminsky|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/03/injury-notes-washington-ball-thybulle-kaminsky.html|access-date=April 4, 2025|website=hoopsrumors.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Alvark Tokyo (2025–present)===
On October 7, 2025, during the pre-season game against the Spurs, Kaminsky made an appearance for [[Guangzhou Loong Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-10-07 |title=Frank Kaminsky: Notches 22 points in defeat |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/frank-kaminsky-notches-22-points-in-defeat/ |access-date=2025-10-09 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}}</ref>

On December 5, 2025, Kaminsky signed with [[Alvark Tokyo]] of the [[B.League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Announcement of new contract with Frank Kaminsky for the 2025-26 season|url=https://www.alvark-tokyo.jp/news/detail/team/id=21005|website=alvark-tokyo.jp|date=December 5, 2025|access-date=December 11, 2025}}</ref>

==National team career==
In November 2019, coach [[Igor Kokoškov]] announced that inviting Kaminsky to the [[Serbia national basketball team|Serbian national team]] was under consideration.<ref>{{cite web |title=Amerikanac u dresu Srbije? |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2019&mm=11&dd=23&nav_id=1621733 |website=b92.net | date=November 23, 2019 |access-date=24 November 2019|language=sr}}</ref><ref name=Wagerbop />

==Personal life==
In July 2023, Kaminsky married sports journalist [[Ashley Brewer]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2023/07/08/ashley-brewer-marries-frank-kaminsky-one-week-after-espn-layoff/|author= Andrew Crane|title=Ashley Brewer marries Frank Kaminsky in Mexico one week after ESPN layoff|website=nypost.com|date= July 8, 2023|accessdate=8 July 2023}}</ref> They have one son together.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kuhagen |first1=Christopher |title=Wisconsin basketball legend Frank Kaminsky welcomes first child with wife Ashley Brewer |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/uw/2025/07/21/frank-kaminsky-wife-ashley-brewer-baby-birth-annoucement-francis-stanley/85289904007/ |website=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel |access-date=22 April 2026}}</ref> Kaminsky is a [[Christianity|Christian]].<ref>{{cite web |title=SS PODCAST: Former Wisconsin & NBA player Frank Kaminsky on growing in faith, becoming a dad |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/podcast/2026/03/27/podcast-wisconsin-nba-frank-kaminsky-faith-dad/ |website=Sports Spectrum |access-date=22 April 2026}}</ref>
